newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity up slightly following physicals.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity up slightly following physicals.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose slightly Monday following a rise in some physical power prices in the U.S. West, industry sources said.
"Some real time prices have risen this morning, and futures seem to be higher on that," said one New York-based electricity broker.
Futures prices were expected to ease later in the day however, on news a California nuclear power station was boosting power, the broker said.
"I think we're going to see this come off yet today," he said.

As of 1215 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were trading up 25 cents at $34.60 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $34.00-34.95, while September was up 29 cents at the day's high of $28.85 after trade as low as $28.50 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 13 cents at the day's high of $23.15 following exchange as low as $22.90, while September was bid at $22.50 from Thursday's close at $22.82 per MWh.
As of 1140 EDT and estimated total of 213 PV and five COB contracts had traded, NYMEX said.

Western physical power prices were reported to be higher Monday morning, with next-day PV peak power said to have traded at $30.50 and $33.25 from Thursday's range of $26.50-28.00 for Saturday and Monday delivery.
Traders said the higher PV prices may have been based on some shortcovering.

In generation news, PG&E Corp's 1,073 megawatt (MW) Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit on the central California coast reached 50 percent power as of early Monday and was expected to hold at that level until midday before resuming power ascension.
The unit is returning from a manual shutdown July 2 that was due to problems with its feedwater system.
The 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was in a startup mode as of early today but had not yet reconnected to the electricity grid.
Moreover, the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit near Phoenix, Ariz., returned to 100 percent output over the weekend after a 15 percent load reduction for repairs late last week.

Almost 2,500 MW of coal-fired generation in the West was scheduled to resume production by today, including two 670 MW Centralia units in Washington, 330 MW Colstrip units in Montana, a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado and a 550 MW Laramie River unit in Wyoming.
Meteorlogists called for wet and cool weather through the Pacific Northwest this week before a warming trend early next week.
Meanwhile, temperatures are projected to average near normal over most of the Southwest but below normal in the far northeast region and above normal in the extreme southwest area.
The 1,070 MW San Onofre 2 was shut June 29 to replace its charge line check valves, and the 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 has been offline since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
San Onofre units 2 and 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively.
As of 1215 EDT, NYMEX Henry Hub August natural gas futures were trading down 2.8 cents at $2.075 per million British thermal units.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
